HAGONOY, Bulacan — More than 300 residents marched through the streets of this municipality early Sunday to mark the first anniversary of Tindig Hagonoy, renewing their call for justice over alleged corruption in flood control projects and for concrete solutions to the town’s chronic flooding problem.
Tindig Kalumpitenyo organized the People’s Rally for the second consecutive year, with more than 300 residents and various groups joining the demonstration.
They vowed that their protest would not end with Sunday’s rally and would continue until their calls for accountability and a lasting solution to the flooding are addressed.

Yuda was among hundreds of residents from various sectors—fisherfolk, tricycle drivers, students, youth groups, professionals, church leaders, persons with disabilities, artists, and fraternity members—who spoke during the Sept. 20 “Black Saturday” protest rally called Tindig Hagonoy.

The protest against corruption gained momentum after Bulacan became the focus of an investigation into anomalous flood control projects in Calumpit, Hagonoy, Baliuag, Malolos, San Jose del Monte City, and Sta.

Organizers said the protests aim to “sound the alarm” to the government and call for the mass arrest of officials allegedly involved in the anomalous flood control projects and other cases of corruption.

The protest was held to raise awareness and demand accountability for the escalating flooding problems in the municipality, amid the controversies surrounding the anomalous flood control projects linked to the Department of Public Works and Highways.

MANILA, Philippines — Hundreds of residents, farmers and fisherfolk waded through flooded roads in Bulacan on Monday, August 31, to protest corruption in flood-control projects and reclamation developments that they blame for worsening the province's chronic flooding.

("The protest by residents, farmers and fisherfolk in Bulacan comes at a crucial time to again demand justice and accountability from all those involved in anomalous and failed flood-control projects, as well as widespread environmental destruction that is submerging communities.") Pamalakaya also pointed to the 2,500-hectare New Manila International Airport development in Bulakan town, which involves reclamation along the Manila Bay coast.

"Farmers and residents of Bulacan have long endured the repeated flooding caused by these useless, anomalous flood-control projects. While corrupt officials and big corporations plunder the public funds and our environment, ordinary people suffer," Ramos said.

A year after Tindig Hagonoy first staged organized a march through flooded streets to protest alleged corruption in flood control projects, Saguinsin said residents are now waiting for the national government to deliver solutions, following assurances from Public Works and Highways Secretary Vince Dizon.
